task.name: Validation is one opaque command plus one advisory string, so nothing can express what a check costs, who may run it, or what its result is worth
task.story_text:
## Why

Validation is one opaque command plus one intermediate command, and that shape has run out.

The gate command is authoritative and complete. The intermediate command dev agents are given is a
single string with no stated relationship to it. Nothing in between can be expressed: which checks are
cheap and which are expensive, which result is advisory and which decides a merge, what a reviewer may
run versus what a developer may, or how a scoped run differs from a complete one. Every question of
that kind currently gets answered by whoever writes the command string, and the answer is invisible to
the system running it.

The cost of the missing structure is already measurable. Gate wall clock was 71.4s at 6,224 tests on
2026-07-27 and the suite has grown since; the gate timeout has been raised twice, 45→60→180, absorbing
growth rather than bounding it. A story touching one package pays for the whole suite on every
iteration and every intermediate cycle. Separately, reviewers were re-running the complete gate
because nothing told them a verdict already existed — a defect fixed on its own, but one that existed
because "who may run what, and what does their result mean" had nowhere to be said.

Two things have been established since this issue was written, and both narrow it.

The seam is real and already load-bearing. Pointing the intermediate command at a project-defined
target that runs the project's lint before its tests removed a class of failure that had stalled four
stories in three days — violations the authoritative gate would reject on, which the intermediate
command never checked. The lint half costs 0.4s against a ~100s suite. That was configuration, not
code, which is the evidence that the boundary belongs where it already is.

Forge already supplies scoping context. A per-story target is substituted into the project's command
today, falling back to a project-declared default. So the mechanism for "forge tells the project what
this run is about, the project decides what to do with it" exists and is unused.

What is missing is not selection. It is that validation has no declared structure and no trust
semantics, so nothing can be said about a result except that a command exited zero.

## Example

What a project can express today, and what it should be able to:

```
today
  gate_command   one string, authoritative, complete, expensive
  test_command   one string, advisory, no stated relationship to the gate

wanted
  a project declares its validation profiles; forge decides when each runs and
  what its result is worth:

    complete    the only result that establishes merge authority
    fast        advisory, for the loop that iterates most
    targeted    advisory, scoped by the context forge supplies

  a project that declares only a complete profile keeps today's behaviour exactly
```

The observable difference is that a result carries what it is worth. A reviewer handed an advisory
result knows not to treat it as a verdict; a merge decision made on a scoped run cannot happen,
because a scoped profile is not the one that carries authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- A project declares one or more named validation profiles, and forge runs the profile appropriate to
  the phase rather than choosing between two fixed command slots.
- Exactly one declared profile carries merge authority. A recorded gate verdict is written only from a
  run of that profile, and a run of any other profile is recorded as advisory.
- A project that declares nothing new keeps its current behaviour. Absent profile declarations, the
  existing gate and intermediate commands are used exactly as they are today.
- Where forge supplies scoping context to a profile, the project's declared command decides what to do
  with it. Forge does not infer test framework syntax, source-to-test mappings, or package layout.
- Where a profile cannot be selected for, or a selection produces nothing, the run widens to the
  complete profile. Unknown and empty inputs cause more validation to run, never less.
- Every validation run records which profile it used and what authority that profile carries, so the
  scope and standing behind any verdict is readable afterwards rather than inferred.

## Out of scope

Impact selection itself, and any caching or reuse strategy. Both are things a project's declared
command may implement, and neither is forge's to build or infer — this issue defines the contract they
would be declared through. Also out of scope: choosing which profiles this repository should declare,
which is configuration work rather than product work.

handoff.summary: Added validation profiles as a typed config layer. A project declares named profiles (complete/fast/targeted) in validation.profiles, each with merge or advisory authority; the loader enforces a closed name vocabulary, non-empty commands, and exactly one merge-authority profile. A new stack-neutral module theforge/validation_profiles.py owns the single selection path: VALIDATE selects the merge-authority profile, dev/fix select targeted then fast, and any unselectable or empty-resolving selection widens to the complete profile. run_gate_full resolves its command through that path and reports the SelectedValidation via a selection_out out-parameter; validate_phase records every run in the new state.validation_runs (profile, authority, resolved command, result, commit, skipped) and writes gate_decisions/last_gate_decision only for merge-authority runs, so a gate_override under declared profiles is recorded as advisory and cannot establish merge trust. Provenance flows through the resume sidecar, the audit record (schema 28 to 29 with a reader-side migration), forge audits rendering, sprint baseline/batch-member records, and both reviewer prompt routes (review_phase and review_pool) via a shared review_context helper. Dev/fix prompts name the selected advisory profile and state that its result does not establish merge authority; absent declarations reproduce the previous prompt text byte-for-byte. Documented in docs/guides/inputs-reference.md and the starter forge.yaml.

acceptance_criteria.notes: select_validation widens on both no-advisory-profile and empty-resolved-command, setting widened=True. Unknown profile names cannot reach selection at all — they are rejected at load, which is the stricter form of the same guarantee.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every validation run records which profile it used and what authority that profile carries, so the scope and standing behind any verdict is readable afterwards rather than inferred.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Every coordinator-executed run records profile+authority: VALIDATE (state.validation_runs, resume sidecar, audit, forge audits, reviewer prompt), the sprint baseline gate (validation_profile/validation_authority in its record), and batch members (copied from the leader). Two transient runs — resume triage in sprint/dag.py and the post-conflict-resolution check in coordinator/workspace.py — select through the same path and name their profile in the verbose log, but persist no record, because neither is story-scoped state. Runs the dev agent performs itself are also not recorded: forge does not observe them, and inventing a self-reported result channel was out of scope for this story.

story_deviations: Profile names are a closed vocabulary rejected at load, rather than an open mapping. The plan accepted arbitrary names and the reviewer flagged that a valid-but-unselectable name would silently never run; a load-time error is the mechanical form of that guarantee.

A story gate_override under declared profiles is recorded as advisory and does not establish merge trust (legacy path unchanged). The plan left override standing open; the AC permits a verdict only from the declared merge-authority profile.
deferred_items: Advisory runs executed by the dev agent itself are not recorded — there is no result channel from the agent's own test runs. Would need a validated dev-handoff result contract.
sprint/dag.py resume triage and coordinator/workspace.py conflict-resolution gates run the merge-authority profile and log it, but persist no validation record.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the two P1s within the approved approach. (1) A passing story gate_override under declared profiles no longer lets a story progress on an advisory result: run_gate_full gained ignore_gate_override, and VALIDATE now widens after a passing advisory run by executing the declared merge-authority profile in the same worktree, resetting selection_out and output_digest first so the recorded selection, stall-brake signature, and gate_decisions entry all describe the verdict-bearing run. The advisory run is still executed and recorded; a failing override does not widen, since it already blocks progression. (2) The _run_gate wrapper gained the same selection_out passthrough, so its two callers record standing: sprint resume triage puts the profile and authority into StoryTriage.reason (the durable record of that decision), and coordinator/workspace.py logs the profile and authority with the post-conflict-resolution gate decision that governs whether an agent-authored resolution lands. Added five tests: widening on a passing override, no widening on a failing one, a story that cannot reach DONE on an advisory result alone, _run_gate selection passthrough, and provenance in the triage reason and the conflict-resolution log. Docs updated to state the widening rule.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The profile selection and provenance work is mostly in place, but advisory validation can still advance a story to DONE and some coordinator-run gates still leave no durable profile provenance. | [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Excellent and highly thorough implementation of validation profiles with robust selection, authority, and audit-visible provenance tracking. | [anthropic-claude-haiku-4-5-cli] Validation profiles implementation is complete and correct. All six acceptance criteria are verified. The design enforces safety mechanically: config-time rejection of invalid profiles, advisory runs provably cannot become verdicts, closed vocabulary prevents silent non-execution, and every verdict-bearing run is recorded with its profile and authority through state, sidecar, audit, and prompts. Backward compatibility is preserved — projects declaring nothing see zero behavior change. Test coverage spans both unit (declaration, selection, widening, scoping) and integration (phase boundaries, resume, audit) with specific tests for failure modes (override does not establish trust, widening works, legacy paths byte-identical). The gate verdict matches.

findings.description: With declared profiles, a story gate override that passes is recorded as advisory but VALIDATE still returns PASS, so REVIEW can approve and the run can reach DONE without any merge-authority validation result.
Conflict-resolution and sprint resume-triage gates run validation and consume the PASS or FAIL result without recording which validation profile ran or what authority it carried.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan's stated profile-name risk is carried. Step 1 accepts a mapping of arbitrary profile names, but Step 2 only recognizes targeted and fast. A valid advisory profile named smoke would load successfully and then never be selected, so Forge would not run a declared profile appropriate to the dev/fix phase.
  Suggestion: Define phase/selection applicability explicitly in each profile declaration, or make the allowed semantic names a validated closed schema. Add a test proving every accepted advisory declaration is selectable or deliberately rejected.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 3-4 provide no data path for advisory results. Current dev/fix prompts only tell the agent which command to run, and src/theforge/devhandoff.py:13-29 has no profile, command result, or authority field. Step 4 then says validation records are populated only from VALIDATE, which always chooses the merge-authority profile. Consequently no non-authoritative run can be recorded as advisory.
  Suggestion: Define how Forge observes advisory execution and its result—such as a coordinator-owned run or a validated dev-handoff result contract—and include the parser/schema/state/audit surfaces and tests needed to record profile, authority, commit, command, and result.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The gate_override risk is not retired. src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:136-145 replaces the configured gate with TaskStory.gate_override, and src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py:755-765 synthesizes PASS/SKIPPED when the override is none. Preserving these as an 'override of the merge-authority path' lets an undeclared custom command—or no command—produce authoritative standing even though the acceptance criterion permits a verdict only from the declared merge-authority profile.
  Suggestion: When profiles are declared, either remove/reject legacy gate_override, map it to a declared profile without changing that profile's command, or ensure override/skip outcomes are explicitly non-authoritative and cannot establish merge trust. Preserve the old override behavior only on the no-profiles compatibility path.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 limits provenance recording to VALIDATE, but authoritative validation also runs through src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1221 and :1290 for baseline gates, src/theforge/sprint/dag.py:937 for reuse triage, and src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:348 after conflict resolution. These call sites are outside the listed recording work, so those runs cannot satisfy the requirement that every validation run records its profile and authority.
  Suggestion: Make gate execution return or emit a common validation-run record and enumerate every production caller that must persist it. Include the sprint baseline/reuse/conflict-resolution audit paths in the plan and tests.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The blast radius for new validation provenance omits two load-bearing callers. src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:2414-2417 copies gate state from a batch leader to each member, so a new validation-record field would otherwise be absent from member audits. Normal reviews build prompts in src/theforge/coordinator/review_pool.py:763-811, not review_phase.py, so changing review_prompts.py and review_phase.py alone will not show profile/authority metadata during ordinary review.
  Suggestion: Add sprint/runner.py and coordinator/review_pool.py to Step 4, copy the authoritative record to batch members, pass it through both normal and review-only prompt paths, and test both flows.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The stated older-record compatibility risk remains carried. The mitigation promises defaults during resume migration and audit rendering, but the plan omits the actual stored-audit migration/rendering surfaces in coordinator/audit_storage.py and coordinator/audit_render.py, and Step 5 does not test an old record with no profile metadata.
  Suggestion: Enumerate the legacy read/migration/render paths that need complete/merge defaults and add a fixture proving an older resume and audit record remain readable and trusted according to legacy semantics.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Blast radius: build_dev_prompt has a caller outside the plan's file list — src/theforge/cli/shared.py:368 (forge run --dry-run) passes only gate_command and no test_command. Likewise build_review_prompt is called from src/theforge/coordinator/review_pool.py:763 and :791, not just review_phase.py:2405. If Step 3/Step 4 add required parameters for profile name/authority, these call sites break at runtime.
  Suggestion: Add the new prompt parameters as keyword arguments with defaults that reproduce today's text (mirroring the existing test_command: str | None = None), or update cli/shared.py and review_pool.py in the same step.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk (plan risk 1, profile-name vocabulary): Step 2's advisory selection keys on the built-in names 'targeted' then 'fast', but Step 1 accepts an arbitrary mapping of profile names. A project declaring advisory profiles under other names gets no advisory selection and silently falls back to the complete profile — correct per the widening AC, but invisible.
  Suggestion: Either constrain declared non-authority profile names to the recognised vocabulary at load time with a clear error, or log which profile was selected and why (including 'no advisory profile matched — widened to complete') so the fallback is readable.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] sprint/runner.py records 'command': config.validation.gate_command in baseline-gate audit dicts at lines 1036, 1061, 1080, 1112, 1160, 1209 and 1517. Once Step 2 resolves the executed command through the merge-authority profile in gate.py, these audit labels can name a different string than the command actually run, weakening the AC-6 readability goal for baseline runs.
  Suggestion: Have the runner report the resolved merge-authority profile command (and its profile name/authority) rather than the raw gate_command field.

finding_registry.description: With declared profiles, a story gate override that passes is recorded as advisory but VALIDATE still returns PASS, so REVIEW can approve and the run can reach DONE without any merge-authority validation result.
Conflict-resolution and sprint resume-triage gates run validation and consume the PASS or FAIL result without recording which validation profile ran or what authority it carried.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
